description: Conflict resolution before upload. Inputs are always: the queued intent, the local row's action time (local_updated_at), and the result of the mandatory Targeted Re-fetch. Output is one decision. FORBIDDEN shortcuts, pinned by the two anti-max cases and by offline-wins cases: (a) Server Always Wins, (b) max(page). Rules R1-R5 are matched in order, first hit wins. `packets` lists the exact wire calls the uploader must make, in order.

rules.R1: refetch says the entity no longer exists -> drop_gone
rules.R2: intent is an explicit MARK_READ / MARK_UNREAD -> upload unconditionally, a remote passive value never outranks an explicit mark
rules.R3: server already equals the intent -> drop_success without sending a packet
rules.R4: progressLastModified is strictly newer than local_updated_at -> drop_remote_wins (latest user action wins, decided by time only). The stamp is ReadProgressDto.lastModified - the progress row's own timestamp, `required` on the wire. BookDto.lastModified must NEVER be substituted: it does not advance when read progress changes, which would make R4 blind to every remote read.
rules.R6: refetch itself failed (transport/auth) -> defer, do not write blind; counted as a retryable failure

cases.name: R5 offline read beats an older, further-along server value (not max(page), not server-wins)
R4 remote action is strictly later -> remote wins even though its page is smaller (not max(page))
R5 the plain offline-reading case: server untouched since our base -> local wins
R2 explicit MARK_READ beats a server value that is strictly newer
R2 MARK_UNREAD is never resurrected by a remote passive progress (this is where max(page) would fail)
R3 already applied - converge without spending a request
R3 does not fire on a completed mismatch: page equal, completed differs
R1 server confirmed the book is gone -> drop the queued action
R6 refetch failed on the wire: never write blind
R6 a rejected credential mid-upload defers without burning attempts
R5 no mirrored server state at all (restored DB, never synced): local intent wins over dropping it
equal stamps are not 'newer': R4 does not fire, so the local action is uploaded

after_success.note: 204 carries no body, so the server stamp is unknown until the next Reconcile. Writing a guessed stamp here would make R4 lie later.
